summary.text: A 27-year-old Black Ethiopian male from a rural part of the Oromia region who farms, with no known chronic medical condition, presented with a 5-day history of periumbilical abdominal pain that later radiated to the right upper abdomen, low-grade fever, palpitations, diarrhea and vomiting. On examination he appeared acutely ill with right upper abdominal quadrant tenderness and no mass found.

Admission investigations were tabulated, and the text states that the erythrocyte sedimentation rate and procalcitonin were increased. Abdominal ultrasonography showed an enlarged subhepatic appendix measuring 6.55 mm in diameter with an internal fecalith 1 cm in depth, and no peri-appendiceal free fluid collection, intraabdominal mass or lymphadenopathy. The diagnosis was subhepatic acute appendicitis.

After intravenous lines were secured for resuscitation and antibiotics and hemodynamic status was stabilized, an appendectomy was conducted, showing an inflamed subhepatic appendix on the verge of rupture. He was discharged after 48 hours without fever, abdominal pain, vomiting or diarrhea, and at a subsequent follow-up was significantly improved with a clean surgical wound.
